q: By the end of 2027, the United States formally revokes its approval of H200-class AI chip exports to China, or lowers the approved volume through regulation, license conditions, or legislation (a de facto halt resulting from Chinese import restrictions or a company's production stoppage does not count)
basis: Approval was announced in December 2025; the January 2026 rule capped volumes at 50 percent of U.S. domestic sales and collected a 25 percent levy in the form of a tariff; in May, licenses were granted to about 10 Chinese companies with a cap of 75,000 units per customer. China blocked imports, then allowed them on a limited basis from August (about 13 percent of the cap). A bill restricting the exports is pending in Congress. The current administration has tightened export controls when the trade truce was faltering and loosened them during truce periods (the H20 was re-approved three months after its 2025 ban), so the path most likely to lead to revocation is retaliation if the truce breaks down · The AI variable in the Taiwan Strait issue
rs: Rules or notices from the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) or the text of legislation, or company disclosures or Reuters reporting
